schema:name: Risk equalization / allocation formulas defined and applied.
schema:description:
A major operational outcome where data-driven mathematical models are deployed to adjust resource distribution based on the specific health risks and demographic profiles of different populations or insurance funds.

Its primary purpose is to level the playing field by sending more money to regions or funds that handle older, sicker, or poorer populations, preventing healthier areas from hoarding wealth while ensuring vulnerable groups are never underfunded.

Example: Under this risk equalization outcome, the national health system applies a new formula that automatically diverts 15% more budget away from a young, wealthy urban district and routes it directly to a rural province with high rates of chronic diabetes, ensuring the rural clinics have enough funding to cover their higher-risk patients.
